item.title: MkDocs Alternatives in 2026: Where Existing Sites Can Go
item.author: xianpeng.shen@gmail.com (Xianpeng Shen)
item.description: The mkdocs package was downloaded 4.3 million times in a single week, yet its last release is from August 2024. An existing site has five ways forward: stay on 1.6.1, upstream 2.0, ProperDocs, Zensical or MkDocs NG. This post compares them with data you can check: whether your plugins run, whether your commands and CI change, build speed, who maintains each one and for how long.

item.title: Six Months of Maintaining MkDocs NG: Why I Keep Going
item.author: xianpeng.shen@gmail.com (Xianpeng Shen)
item.description: Today MkDocs NG 1.11.0 is out: 10 of the 15 most-upvoted open upstream issues are fixed, plugins work without changing their dependencies, and clean builds got a lot faster. Plus how to choose between Sumi and Material, and the new plugin catalog website.

item.title: mkdocs-ng v1.8.0 Released — Upstream Issues Fixed, Builds ~14% Faster
item.author: xianpeng.shen@gmail.com (Xianpeng Shen)
item.description: mkdocs-ng v1.8.0 is out, the first feature release since the fork. Built-in themes no longer copy the entire highlight.js distribution, making clean builds ~14% faster with ~440 fewer files per site. Search finally finds programming keywords like while and if. The next release will bring incremental builds to mkdocs serve.

item.title: mkdocs-ng Maintenance Progress — v1.7.x Fix Summary and Next Steps
item.author: xianpeng.shen@gmail.com (Xianpeng Shen)
item.description: Since taking over mkdocs-ng maintenance, four versions have been released, over a dozen bugs fixed, and the mergedeep dependency removed. The upcoming v1.8.0 will be a feature release, planning to drop support for older Python versions, remove CDN dependencies from built-in themes, and provide a stable Python API.

item.title: Why I Forked MkDocs and Material for MkDocs
item.author: xianpeng.shen@gmail.com (Xianpeng Shen)
item.description: MkDocs has not shipped a release since August 2024, and Material for MkDocs went into maintenance mode in November 2025. I rely on both across my own projects, so I forked them as mkdocs-ng and mkdocs-ng-material. The CLI, mkdocs.yml and plugins stay the same; only the package names change.
